newsitem.title: USA: March US copper center shipments fall 5.4 percent.
newsitem.headline: March US copper center shipments fall 5.4 percent.

text.p: U.S. copper and brass service center shipments fell 5.4 percent in March from February, and the average daily shipment rate dropped by a similar amount, the Copper & Brass Servicenter Association reported.
Shipments of all copper products fell five percent month-to-month, while alloy shipments dropped 5.6 percent. Alloy rod and bar shipments plunged 8.8 percent from February's level, the CBSA reported.
"After the initial quarter of the year, however, servicenters are still doing markedly better than one year ago," the association said.
Total copper shipments in the first quarter are up 9 percent on the same period last year, while alloy shipments are up 3.8 percent, and total shipments up 5.2 percent.
Inventories rose in March, with total copper stocks up 2 percent over February, while alloy sheet, coil and strip product stocks were up 3.9 percent.
Alloy rod and bar inventories were up 7.9 percent.
